question:
Choose the correct meaning of the idiom:

**The icing on the cake**
solution:
The correct answer is '3' i.e. The best part of something .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The idiom **"The icing on the cake"** refers to something that makes a good situation even better or enhances an already positive experience.
 
• It is commonly used to describe an additional benefit or bonus that adds to the overall value or satisfaction.
 
• In this context, it does not relate to a difficult task, a sweet dessert, or a minor detail, but rather signifies **the best part of something**.

Correct Usage: *Winning the championship was amazing, but getting the MVP award was the icing on the cake.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Similar Idioms:**
 
 
• **"Cherry on top":** Refers to an extra detail or feature that makes something already good even better.
 
• **"Crowning glory":** Refers to the most outstanding or beautiful part of something.
